Hi,

A limit order lets you set the maximum price you’re willing to pay (or the minimum price you’re willing to accept) for a contract. Your order will only fill at your limit price or better, and it may fill partially or not at all if the market never reaches your price.

A market order is designed to fill immediately at the best available prices in the order book at that moment. Because it takes whatever liquidity is available, the final fill price can be better or worse than what you expected, especially in thinner markets or for larger order sizes.

When to use each:
- Limit orders: when price matters to you, you’re okay waiting for a fill, or you want to avoid unexpected slippage.
- Market orders: when speed matters most and you’re comfortable with the current available prices (often best for small sizes in liquid markets).

If you tell us which market you’re trying to trade and roughly what size, we can also suggest which order type is less likely to run into slippage.

Best,
Novig Support

Hi,

Thanks for reaching out — happy to clarify how matching works on the order book.

In general, orders match based on the best available price first, and then by time at that price (often called “price-time priority”). That means an order offering a better price will fill before one at a worse price, and if multiple orders are at the same price, the one that was posted first will typically be first in line to fill.

If two people submit the same limit order “at the same time,” the system still records them in a sequence based on when they’re received/accepted by our matching engine, so one will be ahead of the other in the queue at that price level.

If you share:
- whether you’re placing buys/sells (YES/NO) and
- a quick example of the prices/sizes you’re using,
we can walk through exactly how a fill would occur step-by-step.

Best,
Novig Support
